concepts.def: Tall, thin body type — suits long-distance running.
Muscular V-shape body — suits sprinting and rugby.
Wider, softer body — suits sumo or scrum prop.
Ideal weight for an individual and their sport.
Energy intake equals energy used — weight stays stable.
Eating disorder marked by extreme weight loss.

walkthroughs.body_html: Sheldon's three somatotypes: ectomorph (lean — marathon runners), mesomorph (muscular — sprinters, gymnasts) and endomorph (wider — sumo wrestlers, scrum props). Most athletes blend two types.
Optimum weight varies by sex, height, bone structure, muscle mass and sport. A jockey may need a low optimum weight; a heavyweight boxer a high one. There is no universal correct number.

If intake = expenditure, weight is stable. If intake > expenditure, weight rises (fat storage). If intake < expenditure, weight falls. Endurance athletes need high intakes; weight-class athletes carefully manage both.
